lines.say: Your agent is about to run r m dash r f build. Something stops it first.
lines.text: Your agent is about to run rm -rf build. Something stops it first.

lines.say: A mod is a set of JavaScript or TypeScript functions. Claude Code calls them on events, and they can watch, rewrite or answer.
lines.text: A mod is a set of JavaScript or TypeScript functions. Claude Code calls them on events, and they can watch, rewrite or answer.

lines.say: Blast Radius is a sample mod. When Claude calls Bash with a risky command, it holds the call.
lines.text: Blast Radius is a sample mod. When Claude calls Bash with a risky command, it holds the call.

lines.say: It works out what the command would touch. For r m, it lists the files it would delete, with the count and total size.
lines.text: It works out what the command would touch. For rm, it lists the files it would delete, with the count and total size.

lines.say: Two buttons: one proceeds, two cancels. Cancel has the focus, so Enter refuses.
lines.text: Two buttons: 1 proceeds, 2 cancels. Cancel has the focus, so Enter refuses.

lines.say: Claude sees the refusal and the reason, and nothing gets deleted. Every other command runs as normal.
lines.text: Claude sees the refusal and the reason, and nothing gets deleted. Every other command runs as normal.

lines.say: The catch: it reads only the Bash command text. Bash dash c, aliases or eval can slip past. It is a safety net, not a lock.
lines.text: The catch: it reads only the Bash command text. bash -c, aliases or eval can slip past. It is a safety net, not a lock.

data.title: the catch
data.net: reads only the Bash command text

lines.say: Mods are not sandboxed. They run with your permissions, so install only from sources you trust.
lines.text: Mods are not sandboxed. They run with your permissions, so install only from sources you trust.

data.rule: install only from sources you trust

lines.say: Describe a mod to Claude, and it writes one. To try this one, clone claude code playground, then run claude dash dash plugin dir from its mods folder.
lines.text: Describe a mod to Claude, and it writes one. To try this one, clone claude-code-playground, then run claude --plugin-dir from its mods folder.
